prompt: Which statements about Jedis are correct?
explanation: Jedis instances are not thread-safe, so real services pool them; try-with-resources (or a finally block) returns the instance to the pool even when an exception flies; and pipelining is available through jedis.pipelined() followed by sync(). Jedis has no reactive API — that is Lettuce's feature.

options.text: A Jedis instance is not thread-safe and must not be shared across threads
try-with-resources returns a borrowed Jedis to its pool even on exception
Jedis exposes a reactive API on top of its blocking commands
Batched commands can be sent through jedis.pipelined() and flushed with sync()
